subject: [hw] R1 finding F17 (V19, HIGH): narrow/shift loops write Vd before reading all of Vm; Vd==Vm is legal
body:
I confirm T01s overlap finding from the code and from the Arm rule. In emu/n2a32_neon_shift.c:525-560 (do_shift, opc 8/9) the loop reads vec_get(c, mreg, src_esize, i) and immediately vec_set(c, dreg, dbits, i, ...). When the destination overlaps the source (Vd == Vm, which the architecture allows and which compilers use for in-place shifts/narrows), a later iteration reads a lane already overwritten by an earlier one. T01s repro:
  q0 = 0x12345678 x4; vshrn.i32 d1,q0,#8 (dest d1 is the high half of q0)
  expected d1 = 0x3456345634563456; got 0x3456345656343456 (lane 2 corrupted).
The same pattern appears in the other loops that write Vd while reading Vm (VSHLL/VMOVL, the three-different-lengths VADDL/VADDW/VSUBL/VSUBW, VMLAL/VMLSL and the scalar forms); a non-overlapping destination is correct, so this is purely the in-place order.

Fix: copy the 128-bit source (both halves) to a local uint64_t src[2]/uint8_t[16] before the loop and read lanes from that copy, or buffer all result lanes and write after the loop. Please check every loop in the file, not just opc 8/9. Add an overlap case to test_v19 (Vd == Vm and Vd == the high half of Vm) for VSHN/VMOVN/VSHLL/VADDL/VMLAL.

This is F17 in review/r1/FINDINGS.md; V19s verdict goes back to accept-with-findings until fixed. T01 says this is likely the root of k_i8_loop/k_i16_loop/k_i16_mul/k_neon_vmla16/k_neon_vsubl at arm-O2.
